correctness.rationale: Exact Fisher decomposition plus chord-distance Rayleigh bound proves a uniform global ceiling. Maximum evaluation-vector norm and all approaches to its equality are classified; exact chord rationalization gives local Hessian constants. A constructive family reaches the two-term asymptotic, and compactness/subsequence arguments force every maximizer to have the stated square-root separation and midpoint law. The reflected-pair optimum follows from explicit diagonalization. Analytic proof does not depend on numerical optimization; supplementary code verifies symbolic constants, 2500 direct chord formulas and four deterministic-seed searches.

value.rationale: The two-sensor two-mode setting is a natural minimum observable spatial information problem for a heat field measured with positively correlated noise. A sharp singular-noise limit, universal collision coefficient and first-order performance loss jointly identify a non-obvious optimal placement mechanism. The exact reflected-class comparison reveals a 25/16 information loss from imposing a standard symmetry heuristic, supplying a meaningful benchmark for correlated-error sensor-placement methods. It is not a simple renamed classical independent-noise quadrature result; the fixed-correlation modeling limitation is stated explicitly.
